idea.title: The 108-year bottle
idea.summary: A 1906 science-experiment message in a bottle was found on a German island in 2015 and returned, a 108-year wait for one stranger to answer another.
hookOptions: A message waited 108 years for a reader
He never got a reply. She did, 108 years later
sources: Wikipedia: Message in a bottle: oldest message in a bottle, released 1906 by Captain C. Hunter Brown of the Marine Biological Association (drift experiment), found 2015 by Marianne Winkler on Amrum, Germany; Guinness World Record 108 years
Guinness World Records: Longest time for a message in a bottle to be received, 108 years 138 days

scenes.say: A message floated in the sea for 108 years before anyone read it.

scenes.query: Amrum island beach Germany North Sea
scenes.caption: Amrum, Germany
scenes.say: It was thrown in the water in 1906, to track ocean currents.
Inside was a postcard asking whoever found it to send it back.
A woman found it in 2015, on a German beach, 108 years later.
So a stranger finally wrote back, after all that time.

scenes.ask: Who would you send a note to?

post.caption:
A science experiment in 1906 turned into the longest wait for a reply ever recorded. Who would you send a note to? Don't wait 108 years: talk to someone new on randomtalker.com
